# add-greeting: let alpha produce a greeting that beta prints

- size: project
- owner: demo-owner
- repos: [alpha, beta]

## Why

Users of `beta` want a greeting on start-up, and the text belongs in `alpha`,
the shared library, so that other tools can use it too.

## Scope

In: the greeting text in `alpha`; printing it in `beta`.

Out: translations; any change to `gamma`.

### R1 Greeting text
`alpha` SHALL provide the greeting `hello, demo` for a caller that asks for it.

#### R1.S1 Default greeting
- GIVEN `alpha` at the branch head
- WHEN a caller asks for the greeting with no name
- THEN it gets the exact text `hello, demo` (11 characters, no trailing
  newline)

#### R1.S2 Name too long
- GIVEN a name of 65 characters
- WHEN a caller asks for the greeting with that name
- THEN it gets an error naming the 64-character limit, and no greeting

### R2 beta prints the greeting
`beta` SHALL print the greeting from `alpha` as its first line of output.

#### R2.S1 Start-up line
- GIVEN `beta` built against `alpha` at the branch head
- WHEN `beta` starts with no arguments
- THEN its first line of standard output is `hello, demo`, within 1 s of
  start (wall time)

## Approaches

1. Greeting in `alpha`, printed by `beta` (picked: one source of the text).
2. Greeting in `beta` only (rejected: other tools would copy the text).

1. The name limit is 64 characters, counted as Unicode code points.

def checksum(text: str) -> str:
    """The sum of the code points, modulo 65536, in 4 hex digits."""
    return format(sum(map(ord, text)) % 65536, "04x")

## 1 Shape of a project

A project is one Project Space plus the code repos it names. The Project
Space is a git repo holding specs, plans, records and project-level tests. A
code repo holds the project's deliverables: code, its unit tests and the docs
that ship with it. A project whose deliverable is not code (documents, a
paper) has a deliverable repo in the same place, under the same rules.

Put each thing where this table says:

| Thing | Lives in |
|---|---|
| Specs, plans, ledgers, briefs, reports, reviews, evidence, decisions, handoffs, `STATUS.md` | Project Space |
| Project-level tests (acceptance tests for each spec, cross-repo tests, the regression suite of integrated specs) | Project Space |
| Code, unit tests, docs that ship with the code (README, API docs) | Code repo, on branch `change/<id>` until merged |
| Mesh task messages, workflow records, agent and task ids | Mesh bus, never the Project Space |

Never commit a spec, plan, ledger, brief, report, review, evidence record or
project-level test to a code repo. A change's branches hold only code, unit
tests and docs that ship with the code. Commit every process record and every
project-level test to the Project Space.

- Take expected values from outside the code under test: literals,
  hand-checked fixtures, analytical or manufactured solutions, published
  references.

  fail. A test only an intentional decision could fail, such as a message's
  wording, is a change detector; test the behavior instead.

- Put tests in `changes/<id>/tests/`. They stay there until integrate moves

__version__ = "1.0"


def checksum(text: str) -> str:
    """The sum of the code points, modulo 65536, in 4 hex digits."""
    return format(sum(map(ord, text)) % 65536, "04x")

# add-greeting: let alpha produce a greeting that beta prints

- size: project
- owner: demo-owner
- repos: [alpha, beta]
- supersedes: []
- approved: demo-owner 2026-11-01T09:00Z

## Why

Users of `beta` want a greeting on start-up, and the text belongs in `alpha`,
the shared library, so that other tools can use it too.

## Scope

In: the greeting text in `alpha`; printing it in `beta`.

Out: translations; any change to `gamma`.

## Requirements

### R1 Greeting text
`alpha` SHALL provide the greeting `hello, demo` for a caller that asks for it.

#### R1.S1 Default greeting
- GIVEN `alpha` at the branch head
- WHEN a caller asks for the greeting with no name
- THEN it gets the exact text `hello, demo` (11 characters, no trailing
  newline)

#### R1.S2 Name too long
- GIVEN a name of 65 characters
- WHEN a caller asks for the greeting with that name
- THEN it gets an error naming the 64-character limit, and no greeting

### R2 beta prints the greeting
`beta` SHALL print the greeting from `alpha` as its first line of output.

#### R2.S1 Start-up line
- GIVEN `beta` built against `alpha` at the branch head
- WHEN `beta` starts with no arguments
- THEN its first line of standard output is `hello, demo`, within 1 s of
  start (wall time)

## Approaches

1. Greeting in `alpha`, printed by `beta` (picked: one source of the text).
2. Greeting in `beta` only (rejected: other tools would copy the text).

## Open calls

1. The name limit is 64 characters, counted as Unicode code points.
